# Can I Compartmentalise?

> "He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways."
>
> — James 1:8

This is the myth of the two rooms.

It's put about mostly by men on the Willpower Method, who can't stop and so need a story that lets them carry on. The story goes: "That's my private side. It has nothing to do with my marriage, my faith or the man I am at work. I keep it in its box." Dr Jekyll leads the Bible study on Sunday morning. Mr Hyde has the phone at midnight. The two never meet.

It's a neat story, and it is false from top to bottom. In Stevenson's book, Hyde doesn't stay in his room. He gets stronger every time he's let out, and by the end he's turning up without being called. There's only one man in that story, and there's only one of you.

## What you're rehearsing {-}

Every time you do it, you're practising something. Look at what.

You're practising arousal with nobody else there. You're practising being a spectator, with a cast you can swap the instant your interest dips. You're practising getting exactly your own way, at your own speed, with no one else's mood, tiredness or wishes to take into account.

Now set a real woman beside all that. She's one person, and you can't swap her. She has a mind of her own and a bad day of her own. Loving her takes patience and attention, and it means giving something of yourself. In every respect she's the opposite of what you've been rehearsing.

C.S. Lewis saw this long before the smartphone. Of the women a man keeps in his imagination he wrote that "they become merely the medium through which he increasingly adores himself." A sex therapist who treats men for the results says the same thing more drily. Their trouble, he writes, is "a disparity between the reality of sex with their partners and the sexual fantasies". You can't practise that for years in one room and walk into the next room unchanged.

Here is where the two-room story ends up for some men:

> "I now hate sex, do not trust marriage, do not believe in intimacy or falling in love."
>
> — a commenter on a Christian recovery blog

(That man did get free, in his forties. But look what the "private side" did to the rest of the house.)

## The smell of the fryer {-}

The box doesn't even hold during the day. Park beside a burger place with the window down and you've half bought the meal before you've read the menu. The habit wires your day the same way. The empty house, the late hour, the pretty stranger on the train, a bad email from your boss: each one has been linked to the routine so many times that it sets off the itch without asking you. That isn't a private side. It runs all day.

One coach noticed where it leaks out: "you become more anxious in public from what you do in private".

And the box keeps growing. The habit never quite scratches the itch, so the moment one session ends, the next one is already wanted. The drift is always toward more: more often, further over the line, back to the screen you swore off. Only two things hold a man back, and neither is self-control. One is opportunity. The other is a body that can only be flogged so far.

## One man {-}

Human beings rate things. Feed your mind a private cast who are always willing, always new and never tired. You'll start scoring your wife against them, or the wife you haven't met yet. No real woman can beat a harem that's open all night and wants nothing from you.

So no, you can't compartmentalise. Jesus said the same about money, in a line you already know: no one can serve two masters. A man with a secret room has two masters, and the one in the secret room is winning. This is the self-control thread again. **A man who can't control his lust can't be trusted.** The man who thinks he's got it safely boxed is the last to find that out.

Now the good part. The moment the Little Monster is gone, the two rooms become one. That low, shifty, insecure feeling you've carried for years goes with him. You stop managing a double life, because there's only one life left to manage. A man on the NoFap forum, a hundred days out, said it with an exclamation mark: "I don't feel like a creep with a secret perverted second sex life anymore!" Your confidence comes back, and with it a self-respect you may not have felt since you were a boy.

Being the same man in every room is a great deal less work. You'll see.
